#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo (csr mode): CSR insn-match switching on the RVV GEMM workload.
#
# Profiles a KERNEL chosen by csrwi 0x7C0,{0,1} markers in the source. Walks
# one QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 round-trip on rt_c_v_matmul (16x16x16 RVV GEMM):
# QEMU1 seeds A/B, vsim runs the vmatmul_kernel between the markers (the
# measured window), QEMU2 verifies. This is the default switching path a user
# gets out of the box.
#
# Honors all the same env overrides as e2e.sh (VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU,
# VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM, TIMEOUT).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

MODE_LABEL="CSR mode (profiles a kernel)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Fixture: rt_c_v_matmul (RVV 16x16x16 GEMM)"
echo "Trigger: csrwi 0x7C0, 0 (enter) -> csrwi 0x7C0, 1 (exit)"
echo "=========================================================="

set +e
FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=csr EXPECT_RC=0 TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-120}" \
  bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/../e2e.sh"
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -eq 77 ]; then
  echo "[demo csr] SKIP (artifacts missing)"
  exit 77
fi

if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo csr] FAIL ($MODE_LABEL): underlying harness exit $RC"
  exit "$RC"
fi

echo "[demo csr] PASS ($MODE_LABEL)"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end roundtrip harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim -> QEMU 2.
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   EXPECT_RC       Final exit code to assert (default 0).
13	#   TRIGGER_MODE    csr | pc (default csr).
14	#   ROI_START       pc mode only. Switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
15	#                   $VSIM_ELF (default: _hybrid_enter_pc).
16	#   ROI_END         pc mode only. Switch-out PC, same forms
17	#                   (default: _hybrid_exit_pc).
18	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
19	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
20	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
21	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
22	
23	set -euo pipefail
24	
25	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
26	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
27	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"
28	
29	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
30	EXPECT_RC="${EXPECT_RC:-0}"
31	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
32	TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-csr}"
33	
34	hybrid_resolve_paths
35	
36	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
37	NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
38	
39	case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
40	  csr) ;;
41	  pc)
42	    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
43	      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
44	      exit 77
45	    fi
46	    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
47	    # ROI_START / ROI_END (env) name the two switch PCs: each is a 0x address
48	    # or a symbol in $VSIM_ELF. Default to the planted _hybrid_enter_pc /
49	    # _hybrid_exit_pc markers, so existing fixtures need no change.
50	    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
51	    ;;
52	  *)
53	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use csr|pc)"
54	    exit 1
55	    ;;
56	esac
57	
58	# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
59	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
60	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
61	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
62	STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
63	SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
64	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
65	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
66	
67	PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
68	VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
69	if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
70	  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
71	  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
72	fi
73	
74	echo "[$FIXTURE 1/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
75	set +e
76	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
77	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
78	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
79	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
80	  -nographic \
81	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
82	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
83	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" >/dev/null 2>&1
84	QEMU1_RC=$?
85	set -e
86	
87	if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
88	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
89	  exit 1
90	fi
91	
92	if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
93	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
94	  exit 1
95	fi
96	
97	echo "[$FIXTURE 2/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain + spawn QEMU 2"
98	set +e
99	timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
100	  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
101	  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
102	  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
103	  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
104	  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
105	  --qemu-binary "$VSIM_QEMU" \
106	  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
107	RC=$?
108	set -e
109	
110	# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
111	# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
112	# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
113	# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
114	# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
115	if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
116	  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
117	  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
118	  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
119	  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
120	  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
121	  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
122	  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
123	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
124	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
125	    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
126	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
127	      exit 1
128	    fi
129	    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
130	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
131	      exit 1
132	    fi
133	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
134	  fi
135	fi
136	
137	if [ "$RC" != "$EXPECT_RC" ]; then
138	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: expected exit $EXPECT_RC, got $RC"
139	  echo "--- sim log ---"
140	  cat "$SIM_LOG"
141	  exit 1
142	fi
143	
144	echo "[$FIXTURE 3/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] PASS: round-trip exit code $RC"
145

# End-to-end roundtrip harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim -> QEMU 2.
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   EXPECT_RC       Final exit code to assert (default 0).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    csr | pc (default csr).
#   ROI_START       pc mode only. Switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF (default: _hybrid_enter_pc).
#   ROI_END         pc mode only. Switch-out PC, same forms
#                   (default: _hybrid_exit_pc).
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-csr}"

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  csr) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")

    # or a symbol in $VSIM_ELF. Default to the planted _hybrid_enter_pc /
    # _hybrid_exit_pc markers, so existing fixtures need no change.
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use csr|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)

STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e

  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" >/dev/null 2>&1

  exit 1
fi

  exit 1
fi

set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --qemu-binary "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1

set -e

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

if [ "$RC" != "$EXPECT_RC" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: expected exit $EXPECT_RC, got $RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 3/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] PASS: round-trip exit code $RC"

# `./hsim demo csr_oneshot` end-to-end

## 1. Dispatch
- `./hsim demo csr_oneshot` -> `tests/fixtures/demo.sh` row `"T1|demo_csr_oneshot.sh"` -> runs `tests/demos/demo_csr_oneshot.sh`.
- That script just sets env and calls `tests/e2e.sh`:
  - `FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul`
  - `TRIGGER_MODE=csr`
  - `EXPECT_RC=0`
  - `TIMEOUT=120`

## 2. Shared mmap setup (`tests/e2e.sh`)
- Allocates `/dev/shm/vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX` of 128 MB, `truncate`d to size.
- Three temp files: `STATE_QEMU` (drain blob), `STATE_VSIM` (drain blob), `SIM_LOG`.
- This shared file is the DRAM image; both QEMUs and vsim mmap it as the AE350 main memory so `.bss`/heap/stack survive across legs.

## 3. Phase 1 - QEMU1 (functional, fast)
- `qemu-system-riscv64 -M andes_ae350 -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` with the shared mmap as memory backend, ELF as `-bios`, plugin `libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE_QEMU`.
- `main()` runs `init_matrices()`: vectorized `vid.v + vadd.vx + vrem.vx + vse32.v` seeds A and B in `.bss` (located inside the shared mmap).
- `enter_vsim()` macro emits the entry marker `csrwi 0x7C0, 0`.
- The TCG plugin (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) pattern-matches that csrwi at retire, drains the full architectural state (32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, M-mode CSRs, PMP, V block including v0..v31 via `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=64` per reg) into `hybrid_state_v1` at `$STATE_QEMU`, then exits with rc=200.
- Harness asserts rc==200 and `$STATE_QEMU` non-empty.

## 4. Phase 2 - vsim (cycle-accurate, slow)
- Launches `sim_ax45mpv_premium` with `--resume-from-qemu`, `--handoff-out`, `--shared-mem-path` (same `/dev/shm` file), `--qemu-binary` (for handback).
- `handoff_controller` halts hart via DMI, hands `STATE_QEMU` to `ResumeDriver`:
  - Stage v0..v31 bytes into the V-scratch region at GPA `0x00FF0000` in shared mmap.
  - Restore `mstatus.VS`, then PB sweep `vsetvl e8/m1 + vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch.
  - PB `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` to atomically restore `vtype`+`vl`.
  - Abstract-cmd restore `vstart`, `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`, `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret`, FPRs, GPRs.
- Hart resumes at the instruction after the entry marker.
- Runs `vmatmul_kernel()` (outer-product GEMM: per row, `vmv.v.x 0 -> N x vmacc.vx -> vse32.v`) -- this is the measured window.
- `exit_vsim()` emits `csrwi 0x7C0, 1`. Trigger detector halts the hart.
- `StateDrain` reads back all CSRs/GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret via Abstract Commands, then last issues the `vse8.v` PB sweep dumping v0..v31 into scratch; writes `hybrid_state_v1` to `$STATE_VSIM`.

## 5. Cycle accounting
- Before checking RC, harness `od`-reads offsets 624 (`mcycle`) and 632 (`minstret`) from both blobs, prints `kernel_cycles = vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle`. Kernel-window cycle count.

## 6. Phase 3 - QEMU2 (functional, finish + verify)
- vsim's `qemu_handback` spawns a second `qemu-system-riscv64` with the SAME shared mmap (so A/B/C are intact) and NO `-kernel` (memory already has the program).
- Connects via gdbstub, sends P-packet writes for every GPR/FPR/CSR/V-reg (including the full M-mode set + PMP that vsim never touched), pulls v0..v31 back from scratch, then `continue`s.
- Hart resumes after the exit marker. `scalar_matmul_verify()` recomputes A*B in pure C and cell-compares against C left by vsim. Prints `rt_c_v_matmul: PASS` or `FAIL`, exits 0/1.

## 7. Verdict
- `e2e.sh` asserts vsim's exit RC equals `EXPECT_RC=0`, then prints `[rt_c_v_matmul 3/3 mode=csr] PASS`.
- `demo_csr_oneshot.sh` translates rc=77 to SKIP, rc=0 to `[demo csr] PASS`, anything else to FAIL.

The wire format moving between the three legs is `hybrid_state_v1` defined in `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`; the kernel source is `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c:81 vmatmul_kernel()`.

content.text:
`--handoff-out <file>` is the vsim drain destination -- where the cycle-accurate leg writes its `hybrid_state_v1` blob when the exit trigger fires.

Specifically:
- vsim runs until the exit condition retires:
  - csr mode: `csrwi 0x7C0, 1`
  - pc mode: `--hybrid-exit-pc 0xADDR`
  - icount mode: `--hybrid-icount N` insns committed
- On that event `StateDrain` halts the hart and dumps GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the file at this path.
- vsim then exits with rc 200 (mirrors QEMU1's plugin convention).
- The harness reads `mcycle`/`minstret` from offsets 624/632 of this file to compute `kernel_cycles = vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle`.
- If `--qemu-binary` is also set, the same drained struct is fed to QEMU2 over gdbstub before vsim returns.

Without `--handoff-out`, vsim still runs but produces no state file, so neither the cycle accounting nor the QEMU2 handback can proceed -- `e2e.sh` always passes it (`main.cpp:111`, used at `tests/e2e.sh:101`).

content.text:
## Short answer
The orchestrator could absolutely own QEMU2. The state blob is already written to `--handoff-out` before handback runs, so the artifact needed to drive QEMU2 lives on disk. The current in-vsim spawn is convenient, not necessary.

## Why it ended up inside vsim
- The drained state is already in vsim's RAM. Re-reading from disk in a separate orchestrator step is a small redundancy the current code avoids.
- vsim wants to propagate QEMU2's exit code as its own (`qemu_handback.hpp:380`). Doing it in-process keeps that wiring trivial: one `waitpid`, one return value.
- Single timeout boundary. `timeout 120 vsim ...` covers leg-2 and leg-3 together. With an orchestrator-driven split you need two timeouts and tighter error semantics.
- vsim already speaks the gdbstub P-packet dialect (it's the same code path that wires V-CSR transport quirks; see the [[project_qemu_vl_vtype]] vl/vtype fix). Moving it out would mean re-implementing or extracting that client into a standalone tool.

## Why the orchestrator path is cleaner
- Clear three-process layering: orchestrator runs QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2; each leg is a black-box that reads a state file in and writes one out.
- QEMU2 becomes swappable. You could replace it with another QEMU build, an FPGA bring-up tool, or even a real-HW debug agent that speaks gdbstub - vsim wouldn't need to change.
- vsim stops being responsible for forking/execv'ing/waiting on a child it doesn't otherwise care about (`qemu_handback.hpp` is ~390 lines, most of it process management and gdbstub plumbing, not simulation).
- Easier to test. The gdbstub-restore client can be exercised against a canned state blob without needing to run vsim at all.

## Trade-off in one line
In-vsim spawn = one fewer file roundtrip + automatic exit-code propagation; orchestrator spawn = cleaner layering and a swappable phase-3. The orchestrator path is the better long-term shape if you ever want non-QEMU phase-3 backends; the current shape is fine while QEMU is the only target.

If you want, I can sketch what extracting `qemu_handback` into a standalone CLI (`hybrid-handback STATE_VSIM ELF`) would look like before touching code.

content.text:
## Direct answer
**For "skip QEMU2 entirely" the orchestrator-spawn design wins, but only marginally - the current design already handles this cleanly.**

Current vsim already makes QEMU2 optional. `verilator/src/main.cpp:497`:

```cpp
if (exit_code == hybrid::kExitHandoffToQemu && !args.qemu_binary.empty()) {
  ... run_qemu_handback(...)
}
```

If `--qemu-binary` is omitted, vsim drains to `--handoff-out`, returns 200, and exits. No phase 3. So "exit immediately after `exit_vsim`" needs zero new code in vsim - just don't pass `--qemu-binary` in `tests/e2e.sh`.

## Which design fits the use case better

| Concern | vsim-spawn (current) | orchestrator-spawn |
|---|---|---|
| Code path for "no QEMU2" | `if (qemu_binary.empty())` skipped inside vsim | doesn't exist - orchestrator just stops |
| vsim's responsibility | drain + maybe spawn child | drain only |
| CLI surface | `--qemu-binary` optional, conditional semantics | `--qemu-binary` doesn't exist |
| Exit-code propagation when QEMU2 runs | trivial: in-process `waitpid` | orchestrator must read vsim rc, then run QEMU2, then merge codes |
| Exit-code propagation when QEMU2 skipped | trivial: vsim rc is the answer | trivial: orchestrator stops |

For the **skip case alone**, orchestrator-spawn is conceptually cleaner (vsim has one job: drain). For the **run case**, vsim-spawn is simpler (one process tree, one exit code). The current design is the asymmetric compromise: vsim owns both paths because the spawn case dominates the test matrix.

## Recommendation

Don't rearchitect for this. Just expose a knob:

1. Add `NO_QEMU2=1` (or `EXIT_AFTER_VSIM=1`) to `tests/e2e.sh` that drops `--qemu-binary` from the vsim invocation.
2. Add `--no-qemu2` flag to `./hsim run` that forwards the env var.
3. Skip the phase-3 verify in the harness when the flag is set (the `EXPECT_RC` semantics need updating: expect 200, not 0).

That gets you the mode in ~10 lines without touching vsim. If you later want phase-3 to be swappable (FPGA, real HW, alt QEMU build), *that's* when you extract `qemu_handback` into a standalone `hybrid-handback` binary the orchestrator drives - and the no-qemu2 mode falls out for free.

## When to revisit
- If you grow more phase-3 backends (FPGA bring-up, alt QEMU, hardware-in-the-loop), pull `qemu_handback` out and make the orchestrator the coordinator.
- Until then, the current shape with an exposed skip-flag is the cheapest path.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo (pc mode): PC symbol-resolve switching on the RVV GEMM workload.
#
# Same round-trip as the csr demo but the orchestrator resolves
# _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc from the ELF symbol table and
# threads enter_pc=0x... to the QEMU plugin and --hybrid-exit-pc=0x...
# to vsim. The csrwi 0x7C0,{0,1} insns in the binary become inert
# (matchers bypassed; CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on
# andes-ax45mp). Demonstrates that the same GEMM binary can be driven
# without relying on the in-source trigger markers.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

MODE_LABEL="PC mode (profiles a kernel)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Fixture: rt_c_v_matmul (RVV 16x16x16 GEMM)"
echo "Trigger: nm-resolved _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc"
echo "=========================================================="

set +e
FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=pc EXPECT_RC=0 TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-120}" \
  bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/../e2e.sh"
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -eq 77 ]; then
  echo "[demo pc] SKIP (artifacts missing)"
  exit 77
fi

if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo pc] FAIL ($MODE_LABEL): underlying harness exit $RC"
  exit "$RC"
fi

echo "[demo pc] PASS ($MODE_LABEL)"

1	/* Drain markers shared by all C-level round-trip fixtures.
2	 *
3	 * Phase rule:
4	 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
5	 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
6	 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
7	 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
8	 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
9	 *   to register/memory work only.
10	 *
11	 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in
12	 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
13	 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.
14	 */
15	
16	#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
17	#define RT_C_HELPERS_H
18	
19	/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers (CSR 0x7C0,
20	 * uimm 0 = ENTER, uimm 1 = EXIT). Match insn_match.h.
21	 *
22	 * Each helper exposes a global `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc` label co-located
23	 * with the csrwi insn. The labels are inert in CSR mode and consumed by
24	 * the PC-trigger mode driver (resolved via `nm --defined-only`). Because
25	 * each fixture calls each helper exactly once, the labels stay unique. */
26	/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
27	 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
28	 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
29	 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
30	 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
31	 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
32	 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
33	 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
34	/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
35	 *
36	 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
37	 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
38	 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
39	 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
40	 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
41	 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
42	 * consumes the value.)
43	 *
44	 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
45	 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
46	 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
47	 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
48	 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
49	 *     between the markers.
50	 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
51	 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
52	 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
53	 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
54	 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
55	 * attribution. */

61	}

63	{
64	  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl _hybrid_exit_pc\n"
65	                       "_hybrid_exit_pc:\n"
66	                       "csrwi 0x7C0, 1\n" ::: "memory");

 *
 * Phase rule:
 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
 *   to register/memory work only.
 *
 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in
 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.
 */

#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
#define RT_C_HELPERS_H

/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers (CSR 0x7C0,
 * uimm 0 = ENTER, uimm 1 = EXIT). Match insn_match.h.
 *
 * Each helper exposes a global `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc` label co-located
 * with the csrwi insn. The labels are inert in CSR mode and consumed by
 * the PC-trigger mode driver (resolved via `nm --defined-only`). Because
 * each fixture calls each helper exactly once, the labels stay unique. */
/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
 *     between the markers.
 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
 * attribution. */
static inline void enter_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl _hybrid_enter_pc\n"
                       "_hybrid_enter_pc:\n"
                       "csrwi 0x7C0, 0\n" ::: "memory");
}
static inline void exit_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl _hybrid_exit_pc\n"
                       "_hybrid_exit_pc:\n"
                       "csrwi 0x7C0, 1\n" ::: "memory");

It claims to be marker-free but actually uses `rt_c_v_matmul.elf` (markers present, just bypassed) and anchors on labels that only exist because of the marker macros (`rt_c_helpers.h:58-67`). True PC mode should run a binary that has no csrwi markers at all.

## What "PC mode without markers" needs

The markerless build already exists (`rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf`, `Makefile:124-126`), but it runs `GEMM_REPEAT=200` and has no `_hybrid_*_pc` labels. So the demo needs:

1. **A binary**: markerless ELF with whatever repeat count makes sense.
2. **An anchor pair**: real function symbols (not synthetic marker labels).
3. **Trigger semantics**: first-hit only, since the same PC can retire many times.

The natural anchor is `vmatmul_kernel` itself - it's `__attribute__((noinline))` (`rt_c_v_matmul.c:81`), so it has a stable symbol in the ELF.

## Open design questions before I touch code

The cleanest version depends on three calls I need from you:

1. **Which ELF does the demo use?**
   - (a) Reuse existing `rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf` (GEMM_REPEAT=200) -- measures cycles for one kernel call out of 200, since the trigger fires once.
   - (b) New `rt_c_v_matmul_pc.elf` built with `-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -DGEMM_REPEAT=1` -- one kernel call, no markers, simplest semantics.
   - (c) Same source builds both; pc_oneshot uses (b), icount/bbv/slice keep (a).

2. **Enter / exit anchor pair?**
   - `vmatmul_kernel` entry as `ROI_START`. Exit is the trickier one:
     - exit at the function's `ret` PC, or
     - exit at the call site's next insn (`main()` post-call PC), or
     - exit at `scalar_matmul_verify` entry (next function called).

3. **Is the QEMU PC-trigger one-shot?** I haven't verified - if the plugin fires every time the PC retires, anchoring on `vmatmul_kernel` in a 200-rep loop will fire 200 times and break the protocol. Need to confirm before picking option 1(a).

My recommendation: **1(b) + anchor on `vmatmul_kernel` entry / `scalar_matmul_verify` entry**. One kernel call, two unique PCs, no ambiguity. Mirrors the csr_oneshot demo (one measured kernel call) so demos are comparable. Costs: a new Makefile rule and one new ELF target.

Want me to go with that, or pick differently on (1)/(2)?

## Found the loops in `rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf`

Disassembly of `vmatmul_kernel` (note: `init_matrices` and `scalar_matmul_verify` were inlined at -O1; only `vmatmul_kernel` survived due to `noinline`):

```
000000000010021c <vmatmul_kernel>:
  10021c:  vsetivli zero,16,e32,m1,ta,ma   } outer-loop setup
  100220:  vmv.v.i v3,0                    }
  100224-100244: pointer/init setup
  100244:  vmv1r.v v1,v3                   <- outer loop top (reset accumulator)
  100248:  vsetivli zero,16,e32,m1,ta,ma

  10024c:  vle32.v v2,(a5)            <-- INNER LOOP TOP  *** ROI_START ***
  100250:  c.lw    a2,0(a4)
  100252:  vmacc.vx v1,a2,v2
  100256:  c.addi  a4,4
  100258:  addi    a5,a5,64
  10025c:  bne     a5,a1,0x10024c     <-- back-branch (inner loop bottom)

  100260:  vse32.v v1,(a0)            <-- FIRST INSN AFTER INNER LOOP  *** ROI_END ***
  100264:  addi    a0,a0,64
  100268:  addi    a6,a6,64
  10026c:  bne     a0,a7,0x100238     <-- outer loop branch
  100270:  ret
```

## Proposed ROI

| Anchor      | PC          | Insn                |
|-------------|-------------|---------------------|
| ROI_START   | `0x10024c`  | `vle32.v v2,(a5)`   |
| ROI_END     | `0x100260`  | `vse32.v v1,(a0)`   |

Measured window with one-shot triggers: **one full inner-loop traversal** (16 e32m1 iterations of `vle32 + lw + vmacc + addi + addi + bne`). The remaining 199 GEMM_REPEAT calls + 15 outer iterations execute in QEMU2 functionally and don't count toward `mcycle`.

To keep the PCs robust against source changes, derive them dynamically in `demo_pc_oneshot.sh` instead of hardcoding the hex:

1. Run `objdump -d` on `rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf`.
2. Inside the `<vmatmul_kernel>` section: pick the first `vle32.v` PC as `ROI_START`, then the first `vse32.v` PC after it as `ROI_END`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
#
# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.

# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
resolve_pc() {
  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
  case "$boundary" in
    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
  esac
}

# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (defaulting to the planted
#   markers _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc), resolves each against
#   <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare hex). Returns 1
#   and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if either does not
#   resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message (default "pc").
roi_resolve_pair() {
  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
  local start="${ROI_START:-_hybrid_enter_pc}"
  local end="${ROI_END:-_hybrid_exit_pc}"
  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Acceptance test for gemm_modes.md: every demo runs the SAME RVV GEMM
# (rt_c_v_matmul.c), so the suite reads as "one workload, the 4 switching
# modes". Marker-driven demos (csr / pc / archive / simpoint) use the MARKED
# build; count-driven demos (icount / bbv / slice) use the MARKERLESS twin.
#
# Pure parsing of each demo's default FIXTURE -- no artifacts, no round-trip.
# Goes fully green only once F3..F8 have swapped every demo; until then it
# names exactly which demos still point at an old fixture.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

# demo file -> expected default fixture
declare -A EXPECT=(
  [demo_csr_oneshot.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
  [demo_pc_oneshot.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
  [demo_icount_roundtrip.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_bbv_profile.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_archive_replay.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
  [demo_simpoint_loop.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
)

# Pull the default fixture name from the demo's FIXTURE= assignment, whether
# written `FIXTURE=foo ...` (csr/pc inline env) or `FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-foo}"`.
# \K drops everything matched so far, leaving just the fixture token.
fixture_of() {
  grep -oP 'FIXTURE=(?:"?\$\{FIXTURE:-)?\K[A-Za-z0-9_]+' "$1" | head -1
}

bad=0
for demo in "${!EXPECT[@]}"; do
  f="$SCRIPT_DIR/$demo"
  [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "[FAIL] missing demo $demo"; bad=1; continue; }
  got=$(fixture_of "$f")
  want="${EXPECT[$demo]}"
  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then
    echo "[ok] $demo -> $got"
  else
    echo "[FAIL] $demo uses '$got', expected '$want'"
    bad=1
  fi
done

if [ "$bad" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL test_demos_use_gemm: not every demo runs the GEMM yet"
  exit 1
fi
echo "PASS test_demos_use_gemm: all 7 demos run the GEMM workload"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Acceptance test for gemm_modes.md: every demo runs the SAME RVV GEMM
# (rt_c_v_matmul.c), so the suite reads as "one workload, the 4 switching
# modes". Marker-driven demos (csr / pc / archive / simpoint) use the MARKED
# build; count-driven demos (icount / bbv / slice) use the MARKERLESS twin.
#
# Pure parsing of each demo's default FIXTURE -- no artifacts, no round-trip.
# Goes fully green only once F3..F8 have swapped every demo; until then it
# names exactly which demos still point at an old fixture.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

# demo file -> expected default fixture
declare -A EXPECT=(
  [demo_csr_oneshot.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
  [demo_pc_oneshot.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
  [demo_icount_roundtrip.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_bbv_profile.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_archive_replay.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
  [demo_simpoint_loop.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
)

# Pull the default fixture name from the demo's FIXTURE= assignment, whether
# written `FIXTURE=foo ...` (csr/pc inline env) or `FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-foo}"`.
# \K drops everything matched so far, leaving just the fixture token.
fixture_of() {
  grep -oP 'FIXTURE=(?:"?\$\{FIXTURE:-)?\K[A-Za-z0-9_]+' "$1" | head -1
}

bad=0
for demo in "${!EXPECT[@]}"; do
  f="$SCRIPT_DIR/$demo"
  [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "[FAIL] missing demo $demo"; bad=1; continue; }
  got=$(fixture_of "$f")
  want="${EXPECT[$demo]}"
  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then
    echo "[ok] $demo -> $got"
  else
    echo "[FAIL] $demo uses '$got', expected '$want'"
    bad=1
  fi
done

if [ "$bad" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL test_demos_use_gemm: not every demo runs the GEMM yet"
  exit 1
fi
echo "PASS test_demos_use_gemm: all 7 demos run the GEMM workload"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Asserts `derive_inner_loop_roi` (sourced by demo_pc_oneshot.sh) returns the
# first vle32.v PC and the first vse32.v PC after it inside vmatmul_kernel
# of the markerless GEMM ELF. Those are the ROI_START / ROI_END PC mode uses
# to switch around one full inner-loop traversal.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

LIB="$ROOT/tests/lib/inner_loop_roi.sh"
if [ ! -f "$LIB" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: $LIB missing (derive_inner_loop_roi not implemented)"
  exit 1
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
. "$LIB"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || { echo "skip: $ELF missing (run make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf)"; exit 77; }

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip: $OBJDUMP not found"; exit 77; }

read -r START END < <(derive_inner_loop_roi "$ELF" "$OBJDUMP")

if [ -z "${START:-}" ] || [ -z "${END:-}" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: derive_inner_loop_roi returned no PC pair"
  exit 1
fi

if ! awk -v s="$START" -v e="$END" 'BEGIN{exit !(strtonum(s) < strtonum(e))}'; then
  echo "FAIL: ROI_END=$END must come strictly after ROI_START=$START"
  exit 1
fi

START_HI=$(printf '0x%x' $((START + 4)))
END_HI=$(printf '0x%x' $((END + 4)))

if ! "$OBJDUMP" -d --start-address="$START" --stop-address="$START_HI" "$ELF" \
    | grep -qE "^[[:space:]]*[0-9a-f]+:[[:space:]]+[0-9a-f]+[[:space:]]+vle32\.v\b"; then
  echo "FAIL: ROI_START=$START is not a vle32.v insn"
  exit 1
fi
if ! "$OBJDUMP" -d --start-address="$END" --stop-address="$END_HI" "$ELF" \
    | grep -qE "^[[:space:]]*[0-9a-f]+:[[:space:]]+[0-9a-f]+[[:space:]]+vse32\.v\b"; then
  echo "FAIL: ROI_END=$END is not a vse32.v insn"
  exit 1
fi

echo "PASS test_demo_pc_oneshot_inner_loop: ROI_START=$START (vle32.v) ROI_END=$END (vse32.v)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo (pc mode): PC-trigger switching anchored on the GEMM inner-loop
# boundary - no source-level markers, no synthetic _hybrid_*_pc labels.
#
# Runs the markerless GEMM twin (rt_c_v_matmul_free, built with
# -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -DGEMM_REPEAT=200). At launch the script objdumps the
# ELF, picks the first vle32.v PC and the first vse32.v PC after it inside
# vmatmul_kernel, and threads them to the QEMU plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim
# (--hybrid-exit-pc). Triggers are one-shot on both legs (plugin exits on
# first match; vsim drains on first match), so the measured window is one
# full inner-loop traversal of the first GEMM call.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/tests/lib/inner_loop_roi.sh"

MODE_LABEL="PC mode (markerless, innermost loop)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Fixture: rt_c_v_matmul_free (markerless GEMM twin, GEMM_REPEAT=200)"
echo "Trigger: objdump-derived vle32.v / vse32.v in vmatmul_kernel"
echo "=========================================================="

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf"
if [ ! -f "$ELF" ]; then
  echo "[demo pc] SKIP: $ELF missing (run make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf)"
  exit 77
fi

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
if ! command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[demo pc] SKIP: objdump not found at $OBJDUMP"
  exit 77
fi

read -r ROI_START ROI_END < <(derive_inner_loop_roi "$ELF" "$OBJDUMP") || true
if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] || [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
  echo "[demo pc] FAIL: could not derive inner-loop PCs from $ELF"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Derived ROI: vle32.v @ $ROI_START -> vse32.v @ $ROI_END"

set +e

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Acceptance test for gemm_modes.md: every demo runs the SAME RVV GEMM
# (rt_c_v_matmul.c), so the suite reads as "one workload, the 4 switching
# modes". Marker-driven demos (csr / pc / archive / simpoint) use the MARKED
# build; count-driven demos (icount / bbv / slice) use the MARKERLESS twin.
#
# Pure parsing of each demo's default FIXTURE -- no artifacts, no round-trip.
# Goes fully green only once F3..F8 have swapped every demo; until then it
# names exactly which demos still point at an old fixture.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

# demo file -> expected default fixture
declare -A EXPECT=(
  [demo_csr_oneshot.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
  [demo_pc_oneshot.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_icount_roundtrip.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_bbv_profile.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_archive_replay.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
  [demo_simpoint_loop.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
)

# Pull the default fixture name from the demo's FIXTURE= assignment, whether
# written `FIXTURE=foo ...` (csr/pc inline env) or `FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-foo}"`.
# \K drops everything matched so far, leaving just the fixture token.
fixture_of() {
  grep -oP 'FIXTURE=(?:"?\$\{FIXTURE:-)?\K[A-Za-z0-9_]+' "$1" | head -1
}

bad=0
for demo in "${!EXPECT[@]}"; do
  f="$SCRIPT_DIR/$demo"
  [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "[FAIL] missing demo $demo"; bad=1; continue; }
  got=$(fixture_of "$f")
  want="${EXPECT[$demo]}"
  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then
    echo "[ok] $demo -> $got"
  else
    echo "[FAIL] $demo uses '$got', expected '$want'"
    bad=1
  fi
done

if [ "$bad" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL test_demos_use_gemm: not every demo runs the GEMM yet"
  exit 1
fi
echo "PASS test_demos_use_gemm: all 7 demos run the GEMM workload"

### 4.2 PC mode - markerless GEMM, inner-loop boundary from objdump

Same workload as CSR mode, but the binary carries **no** trigger markers and
the switch PCs are computed at demo launch by disassembling the ELF.

```sh
bash tests/demos/demo_pc_oneshot.sh
```

The demo runs `rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf` - the **markerless twin** of the GEMM
fixture, built `-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -DGEMM_REPEAT=200` from the same source as
the marked `rt_c_v_matmul`. `tests/lib/inner_loop_roi.sh::derive_inner_loop_roi`
objdumps the ELF, picks the first `vle32.v` PC inside `vmatmul_kernel` as
`ROI_START` and the first `vse32.v` PC after it as `ROI_END`. Both triggers
are one-shot (QEMU plugin `exit(200)` on first match; vsim drains on first
match), so the measured window is **one full inner-loop traversal** of the
first GEMM call.

The mechanism is fully general - pc mode can target **any** symbol or raw
address. Override either boundary:

```sh
./hsim run <elf> --mode pc --roi-start <sym|0xADDR> --roi-end <sym|0xADDR>
```

Under `tests/e2e.sh` the same knobs are the `ROI_START` / `ROI_END` env vars
(each a symbol name or `0x` address; unset -> the legacy
`_hybrid_enter_pc` / `_hybrid_exit_pc` defaults for asm fixtures that still
plant labels).

To see what the demo passes under the hood:

```sh
OBJDUMP=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
. tests/lib/inner_loop_roi.sh
read -r ROI_START ROI_END < <(derive_inner_loop_roi \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf "$OBJDUMP")
echo "enter=$ROI_START  exit=$ROI_END"   # e.g. 0x10024c / 0x100260

# QEMU1 leg
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=/dev/shm/share,size=134217728 \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=/tmp/q1.bin,enter_pc=$ROI_START"

# vsim leg
"$VSIM_BIN" tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
  --resume-from-qemu /tmp/q1.bin \
  --handoff-out /tmp/v.bin \
  --shared-mem-path /dev/shm/share \
  --shared-mem-size 134217728 \
  --qemu-binary "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  --hybrid-exit-pc "$ROI_END"
```

The fixture binary differs from CSR mode (markerless vs marked) and the
orchestrator arguments carry hex PCs instead of CSR-trigger plumbing.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo (pc mode): PC-trigger switching anchored on the GEMM inner-loop
# boundary - no source-level markers, no synthetic _hybrid_*_pc labels.
#
# Runs the markerless GEMM twin (rt_c_v_matmul_free, built with
# -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -DGEMM_REPEAT=200). At launch the script objdumps the
# ELF, picks the first vle32.v PC and the first vse32.v PC after it inside
# vmatmul_kernel, and threads them to the QEMU plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim
# (--hybrid-exit-pc). Triggers are one-shot on both legs (plugin exits on
# first match; vsim drains on first match), so the measured window is one
# full inner-loop traversal of the first GEMM call.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/tests/lib/inner_loop_roi.sh"

MODE_LABEL="PC mode (markerless, innermost loop)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Fixture: rt_c_v_matmul_free (markerless GEMM twin, GEMM_REPEAT=200)"
echo "Trigger: objdump-derived vle32.v / vse32.v in vmatmul_kernel"
echo "=========================================================="

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf"
if [ ! -f "$ELF" ]; then
  echo "[demo pc] SKIP: $ELF missing (run make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf)"
  exit 77
fi

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
if ! command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[demo pc] SKIP: objdump not found at $OBJDUMP"
  exit 77
fi

read -r ROI_START ROI_END < <(derive_inner_loop_roi "$ELF" "$OBJDUMP") || true
if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] || [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
  echo "[demo pc] FAIL: could not derive inner-loop PCs from $ELF"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Derived ROI: vle32.v @ $ROI_START -> vse32.v @ $ROI_END"

set +e
FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul_free TRIGGER_MODE=pc EXPECT_RC=0 \
  ROI_START="$ROI_START" ROI_END="$ROI_END" \
  TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-120}" \
  bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/../e2e.sh"
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -eq 77 ]; then
  echo "[demo pc] SKIP (artifacts missing)"
  exit 77
fi

if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo pc] FAIL ($MODE_LABEL): underlying harness exit $RC"
  exit "$RC"
fi

echo "[demo pc] PASS ($MODE_LABEL)"

 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,

 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.

#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
#define RT_C_HELPERS_H

/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers (CSR 0x7C0,
 * uimm 0 = ENTER, uimm 1 = EXIT). Match insn_match.h.
 *
 * Each helper exposes a global `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc` label co-located
 * with the csrwi insn. The labels are inert in CSR mode and consumed by
 * the PC-trigger mode driver (resolved via `nm --defined-only`). Because
 * each fixture calls each helper exactly once, the labels stay unique. */
/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
 *     between the markers.
 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
 * attribution. */
static inline void enter_vsim(void)
{

                       "_hybrid_enter_pc:\n"
                       "csrwi 0x7C0, 0\n" ::: "memory");
}
static inline void exit_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl _hybrid_exit_pc\n"
                       "_hybrid_exit_pc:\n"
                       "csrwi 0x7C0, 1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

/* Drain markers shared by all C-level round-trip fixtures.
 *
 * Phase rule:
 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
 *   to register/memory work only.
 *
 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in
 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.
 */

#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
#define RT_C_HELPERS_H

/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers (CSR 0x7C0,
 * uimm 0 = ENTER, uimm 1 = EXIT). Match insn_match.h.
 *
 * CSR mode pattern-matches the csrwi insns directly; the helpers do not
 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger demos derive their switch
 * PCs at runtime (see tests/lib/inner_loop_roi.sh for the GEMM case)
 * instead of relying on planted labels. */
/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
 *     between the markers.
 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
 * attribution. */
static inline void enter_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("_hybrid_enter_pc:\n"
                       "csrwi 0x7C0, 0\n" ::: "memory");
}
static inline void exit_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("_hybrid_exit_pc:\n"
                       "csrwi 0x7C0, 1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

def cmd_demo(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    if not args.selector:
        print(
            "hsim: missing demo selector -- run ./hsim list demos",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2

    short, script = _resolve_demo(args.selector)
    if script is None:
        print(
            f"hsim: unknown demo: {args.selector} -- "
            "run ./hsim list demos (or use T1..T7)",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2
    if not script.is_file():
        print(f"hsim: demo script not found: {script}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    env_extra = _parse_demo_passthrough(args.extras)
    if env_extra is None:
        print(
            "hsim: passthrough args must be KEY=VAL form (after `--`)",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2

    artifacts = _resolve_artifacts()
    for label, path in artifacts.items():
        if not path.is_file():
            print(f"hsim: {label} not built -- run ./hsim build", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2

    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["VSIM_BIN"]    = str(artifacts["vsim"])
    env["VSIM_QEMU"]   = str(artifacts["qemu"])
    env["VSIM_PLUGIN"] = str(artifacts["plugin"])
    env.update(env_extra)

/* Drain markers shared by all C-level round-trip fixtures.
 *
 * Phase rule:
 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
 *   to register/memory work only.
 *
 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in
 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.
 */

#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
#define RT_C_HELPERS_H

/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers (CSR 0x7C0,
 * uimm 0 = ENTER, uimm 1 = EXIT). Match insn_match.h.
 *
 * CSR mode pattern-matches the csrwi insns directly; the helpers do not
 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger demos derive their switch
 * PCs at runtime (see tests/lib/inner_loop_roi.sh for the GEMM case)
 * instead of relying on planted labels. */
/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
 *     between the markers.
 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
 * attribution. */
static inline void enter_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("csrwi 0x7C0, 0\n" ::: "memory");
}
static inline void exit_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("csrwi 0x7C0, 1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

Yes - 22808 vs 1028 lines up cleanly. Quick decomposition:

**CSR (rt_c_v_matmul, GEMM_REPEAT=1): 22808 cycles**
- Covers full `vmatmul_kernel()`: 16 outer rows
- Per row: `vsetvli` + `vmv.v.x 0` + (16x inner k-loop) + `vse32.v` + outer branch
- 22808 / 16 = **~1425 cycles per row**

**PC (rt_c_v_matmul_free): 1028 cycles**
- Covers `[first vle32.v ... first vse32.v)` in `vmatmul_kernel` -> exactly **one inner k-loop traversal** of the i=0 row (no prologue, no vse32, no outer branch)
- 1028 / 16 inner iterations = **~64 cycles per inner iter** (scalar load + `vle32.v` + `vmacc.vx` + ptr incr + branch)

**Cross-check**: 1425 (per-row, CSR) - 1028 (inner k-loop only, PC) = **~397 cycles per row of non-inner overhead** (`vmv` reset + `vse32.v` of 16 elts + outer loop ctl + function prologue amortized). Plausible.

So:
- **CSR ≈ 16 x PC + per-row overhead.** Matches structure exactly.
- GEMM_REPEAT=200 in the markerless ELF doesn't inflate PC: the trigger is one-shot, drains on the very first `vle32.v`/`vse32.v` pair, so the 199 extra GEMM iterations never execute on vsim.

**Zero full GEMMs.** PC mode never gets near GEMM_REPEAT=200.

Trigger is one-shot. The drain fires the very first time the hart retires `vle32.v` at 0x10024c, then again the first time it hits `vse32.v` at 0x100260. That happens inside the **first** GEMM call (`rep=0`), at **i=0** of `vmatmul_kernel`, after the **first** complete inner k loop (k=0..15).

So vsim actually executes:
- `rep` outer iterations: **partial (0 completed)**
- `i` outer rows: **partial (0 completed)**
- `k` inner iterations: **16 (one full inner loop of i=0, rep=0)**
- `vse32.v`: **0** (drain fires at its PC before retire; see `state_drain` semantics)

The other 199 GEMM_REPEAT iterations exist only in the markerless ELF to give count-driven modes (icount / bbv / slice) a long marker-free instruction stream to sample. PC mode ignores them entirely.

Yes - pick the PCs at the call boundary instead of inside the inner loop.

**Concrete derivation (markerless ELF):**
- `start_pc` = symbol address of `vmatmul_kernel` (function entry)
- `end_pc`   = PC of the instruction **after** the `jal vmatmul_kernel` in `main` (the call-return site)

Both are dynamic via objdump/nm:
- `nm rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf | awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print $1}'` -> start
- objdump main's body, find `jal <vmatmul_kernel>`, take the next line's address -> end

**What vsim executes with this range:**
- One full `vmatmul_kernel()` call (16 rows x 16 inner iters + prologue/epilogue + vse32 stores)
- Drain fires when control returns to main and is about to retire the post-jal insn
- One-shot: rep=0 only; reps 1..199 never run

Cycle count should land **~22808** (matching csr_oneshot on `rt_c_v_matmul`), within drain/csrwi overhead.

**Tradeoff vs. inner-loop ROI:**

| Aspect            | Inner-loop ROI (current)        | Kernel-call ROI (proposed)          |
|-------------------|---------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Window            | 16 inner k iters of i=0         | Full vmatmul_kernel (16 rows)       |
| Useful for        | Steady-state inner-loop IPC     | Whole-kernel cycle estimate         |
| Equivalent to     | A slice of CSR mode             | CSR mode (without the csrwi insns)  |
| Inner code change | None                            | None                                |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
#
# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.

# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
resolve_pc() {
  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
  case "$boundary" in
    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
  esac
}

# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (defaulting to the planted
#   markers _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc), resolves each against
#   <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare hex). Returns 1
#   and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if either does not
#   resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message (default "pc").
roi_resolve_pair() {
  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
  local start="${ROI_START:-_hybrid_enter_pc}"
  local end="${ROI_END:-_hybrid_exit_pc}"
  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# derive_kernel_roi: derive the PC pair that frames one full call of the
# vsim-phase kernel (vmatmul_kernel) in an ELF, with no source-level
# markers required.
#
#   start_pc = symbol address of vmatmul_kernel (function entry)
#   end_pc   = PC of the instruction immediately following the
#              `jal ...<vmatmul_kernel>` site inside main (call-return PC)
#
# Used by PC-trigger demos against the markerless GEMM twin: the QEMU
# plugin's one-shot enter trigger fires when the hart retires the first
# insn at vmatmul_kernel; vsim's one-shot exit trigger fires when the hart
# is about to retire the post-jal insn in main. The measured window is
# therefore exactly one vmatmul_kernel call (16 outer rows x 16 inner
# k-iterations + prologue/epilogue + 16 vse32 stores), regardless of how
# many times main's GEMM_REPEAT loop is configured to invoke the kernel.
#
# Usage:
#   . tests/lib/kernel_roi.sh
#   read -r START END < <(derive_kernel_roi <elf> <objdump> <nm>)
#
# On success prints "0x<start> 0x<end>" (single line, space-separated) and
# returns 0. On miss prints nothing and returns 1.

derive_kernel_roi() {
  local elf="$1" objdump="$2" nm="$3"

  local start
  start=$("$nm" --defined-only "$elf" 2>/dev/null \
    | awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print $1; exit}')
  [ -n "$start" ] || return 1

  local end
  end=$("$objdump" -d "$elf" 2>/dev/null | awk '
    /^[0-9a-f]+ <main>:/             { in_main = 1; next }
    in_main && /^[0-9a-f]+ <[^>]+>:/ { in_main = 0 }
    in_main && saw_call              { sub(":", "", $1); print $1; exit }
    in_main && $3 == "jal" && index($0, "<vmatmul_kernel>") { saw_call = 1 }
  ')
  [ -n "$end" ] || return 1

  printf '0x%s 0x%s\n' "$start" "$end"
}

# insn at vmatmul_kernel; vsim's one-shot exit trigger fires when the hart
# is about to retire the post-jal insn in main. The measured window is
# therefore exactly one vmatmul_kernel call (16 outer rows x 16 inner
# k-iterations + prologue/epilogue + 16 vse32 stores), regardless of how
# many times main's GEMM_REPEAT loop is configured to invoke the kernel.
#
# Usage:
#   . tests/lib/kernel_roi.sh
#   read -r START END < <(derive_kernel_roi <elf> <objdump> <nm>)
#
# On success prints "0x<start> 0x<end>" (single line, space-separated) and
# returns 0. On miss prints nothing and returns 1.

derive_kernel_roi() {
  local elf="$1" objdump="$2" nm="$3"

  local start
  start=$("$nm" --defined-only "$elf" 2>/dev/null \
    | awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print $1; exit}')
  [ -n "$start" ] || return 1

  local end
  end=$("$objdump" -d "$elf" 2>/dev/null | awk '
    /^[0-9a-f]+ <main>:/             { in_main = 1; next }
    in_main && /^[0-9a-f]+ <[^>]+>:/ { in_main = 0 }
    in_main && saw_call              { sub(":", "", $1); print $1; exit }
    in_main && $3 == "jal" && index($0, "<vmatmul_kernel>") { saw_call = 1 }
  ')
  [ -n "$end" ] || return 1

  printf '0x%s 0x%s\n' "$start" "$end"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# derive_kernel_roi: derive the PC pair that frames one full call of the
# vsim-phase kernel (vmatmul_kernel) in an ELF, with no source-level
# markers required.
#
#   start_pc = symbol address of vmatmul_kernel (function entry)
#   end_pc   = PC of the instruction immediately following the
#              `jal ...<vmatmul_kernel>` site inside main (call-return PC)
#
# Used by PC-trigger demos against the markerless GEMM twin: the QEMU
# plugin's one-shot enter trigger fires when the hart retires the first
# insn at vmatmul_kernel; vsim's one-shot exit trigger fires when the hart
# is about to retire the post-jal insn in main. The measured window is
# therefore exactly one vmatmul_kernel call (16 outer rows x 16 inner
# k-iterations + prologue/epilogue + 16 vse32 stores), regardless of how
# many times main's GEMM_REPEAT loop is configured to invoke the kernel.
#
# Usage:
#   . tests/lib/kernel_roi.sh
#   read -r START END < <(derive_kernel_roi <elf> <objdump> <nm>)
#
# On success prints "0x<start> 0x<end>" (single line, space-separated) and
# returns 0. On miss prints nothing and returns 1.
#
# Implementation note: outputs are captured to variables first, then fed
# to awk via here-string. This avoids `cmd | awk '... exit'` pipes, which
# trigger SIGPIPE on the upstream producer and abort the caller when
# `set -o pipefail` is active.

derive_kernel_roi() {
  local elf="$1" objdump="$2" nm="$3"
  local nm_out obj_out start end

  nm_out=$("$nm" --defined-only "$elf" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  obj_out=$("$objdump" -d "$elf" 2>/dev/null) || return 1

  start=$(awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print $1; exit}' <<< "$nm_out")
  [ -n "$start" ] || return 1

  end=$(awk '
    /^[0-9a-f]+ <main>:/             { in_main = 1; next }
    in_main && /^[0-9a-f]+ <[^>]+>:/ { in_main = 0 }
    in_main && saw_call              { sub(":", "", $1); print $1; exit }
    in_main && $3 == "jal" && index($0, "<vmatmul_kernel>") { saw_call = 1 }
  ' <<< "$obj_out")
  [ -n "$end" ] || return 1

  printf '0x%s 0x%s\n' "$start" "$end"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# derive_kernel_roi: derive the PC pair that frames one full call of the
# vsim-phase kernel (vmatmul_kernel) in an ELF, with no source-level
# markers required.
#
#   start_pc = symbol address of vmatmul_kernel (function entry)
#   end_pc   = PC of the instruction immediately following the
#              `jal ...<vmatmul_kernel>` site inside main (call-return PC)
#
# Used by PC-trigger demos against the markerless GEMM twin: the QEMU
# plugin's one-shot enter trigger fires when the hart retires the first
# insn at vmatmul_kernel; vsim's one-shot exit trigger fires when the hart
# is about to retire the post-jal insn in main. The measured window is
# therefore exactly one vmatmul_kernel call (16 outer rows x 16 inner
# k-iterations + prologue/epilogue + 16 vse32 stores), regardless of how
# many times main's GEMM_REPEAT loop is configured to invoke the kernel.
#
# Usage:
#   . tests/lib/kernel_roi.sh
#   read -r START END < <(derive_kernel_roi <elf> <objdump> <nm>)
#
# On success prints "0x<start> 0x<end>" (single line, space-separated) and
# returns 0. On miss prints nothing and returns 1.

derive_kernel_roi() {
  local elf="$1" objdump="$2" nm="$3"

  local start
  start=$("$nm" --defined-only "$elf" 2>/dev/null \
    | awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print $1; exit}')
  [ -n "$start" ] || return 1

  local end
  end=$("$objdump" -d "$elf" 2>/dev/null | awk '
    /^[0-9a-f]+ <main>:/             { in_main = 1; next }
    in_main && /^[0-9a-f]+ <[^>]+>:/ { in_main = 0 }
    in_main && saw_call              { sub(":", "", $1); print $1; exit }
    in_main && $3 == "jal" && index($0, "<vmatmul_kernel>") { saw_call = 1 }
  ')
  [ -n "$end" ] || return 1

  printf '0x%s 0x%s\n' "$start" "$end"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo (pc mode): PC-trigger switching anchored on the GEMM kernel
# boundary - no source-level markers, no synthetic _hybrid_*_pc labels.
#
# Runs the markerless GEMM twin (rt_c_v_matmul_free, built with
# -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -DGEMM_REPEAT=200). At launch the script derives
# two PCs from the ELF: the symbol address of vmatmul_kernel (function
# entry) and the address of the instruction immediately following the
# `jal vmatmul_kernel` site in main (call-return). They thread to the
# QEMU plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim (--hybrid-exit-pc). Triggers are
# one-shot on both legs (plugin exits on first match; vsim drains on
# first match), so the measured window is exactly one full
# vmatmul_kernel call, regardless of GEMM_REPEAT.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/tests/lib/kernel_roi.sh"

MODE_LABEL="PC mode (markerless, whole kernel)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Fixture: rt_c_v_matmul_free (markerless GEMM twin, GEMM_REPEAT=200)"
echo "Trigger: ELF-derived vmatmul_kernel entry -> post-jal return PC"

content.text:
Holding the commit until you confirm scope.

**Why GEMM_REPEAT=200:** it's set on the markerless twin so the **count-driven modes** (icount / bbv / slice) have a long marker-free instruction stream to sample. PC mode just **reuses the same ELF** rather than building a separate markerless build per mode.

From `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c:34-41`:

```c
/* The marked build (default, GEMM_REPEAT=1) runs the GEMM once between
 * the drain markers. The markerless twin (-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
 * -DGEMM_REPEAT=K) drops the markers and runs K back-to-back GEMMs,
 * lengthening the instruction stream so the count-driven modes
 * (icount / bbv / slice) have a long, marker-free window to sample.
 * Each kernel call re-seeds its accumulator and overwrites C, so
 * repeating is idempotent. */
```

**For PC mode specifically: GEMM_REPEAT is irrelevant.** The one-shot trigger drains during the first `vmatmul_kernel` call, so reps 1..199 never execute. We could drop it to 1 for PC mode alone, but then we'd ship two markerless ELFs instead of one. Single shared markerless artifact is the cheaper choice.

Want me to proceed with the commit?

echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"

echo "ROI end_pc   = $ROI_END  (insn after jal vmatmul_kernel in main)"

cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
behavioral: pc demo goes markerless; measures one full vmatmul_kernel

Switch tests/demos/demo_pc_oneshot.sh from the marked rt_c_v_matmul to the
markerless rt_c_v_matmul_free twin and derive both switch PCs from the ELF
at launch. New tests/lib/kernel_roi.sh::derive_kernel_roi reads
vmatmul_kernel's entry PC from `nm` and the address of the instruction
immediately following `jal vmatmul_kernel` in main from objdump. Both
triggers are one-shot, so the measured window is exactly one full kernel
call regardless of the binary's GEMM_REPEAT setting.

Strip every `.globl _hybrid_*_pc` directive and label line from the .S
fixtures and from runtime/rt_c_helpers.h. With the PC demo now deriving
its boundaries from the ELF instead of resolving planted symbols, the
labels were dead in every fixture; removing them keeps the markerless
promise honest. test_no_hybrid_pc_labels.sh is the permanent guard that
no fixture re-introduces them, and test_demo_pc_oneshot_kernel.sh checks
derive_kernel_roi against an independent ground-truth pass over nm /
objdump.

Cleanup wins along the way:
- hsim demo subcmd injects HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN from config.env when not in
  env, so `./hsim demo pc_oneshot` finds objdump/nm without `source
  setup.sh` first.
- tests/lib/roi.sh and roi.test.sh were already required by HEAD's
  tests/e2e.sh but had been left untracked; bring them in so a fresh
  checkout runs.
- USER_GUIDE.md section 4.2 retitled "markerless GEMM, whole-kernel
  boundary from ELF" with the matching code example.

Cycle check: PC mode reports 22747 cycles vs CSR mode's 22808 on the
same 16x16x16 RVV GEMM (within 0.3%), confirming the ELF-derived PCs
bound exactly the same kernel ROI as the source-level csrwi markers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
