#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo (pc mode): PC-trigger switching anchored on the GEMM kernel
# boundary - no source-level markers, no synthetic _hybrid_*_pc labels.
#
# Runs the markerless GEMM twin (rt_c_v_matmul_free, built with
# -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -DGEMM_REPEAT=200). At launch the script derives
# two PCs from the ELF: the symbol address of vmatmul_kernel (function
# entry) and the address of the instruction immediately following the
# `jal vmatmul_kernel` site in main (call-return). They thread to the
# QEMU plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim (--hybrid-exit-pc). Triggers are
# one-shot on both legs (plugin exits on first match; vsim drains on
# first match), so the measured window is exactly one full
# vmatmul_kernel call, regardless of GEMM_REPEAT.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/tests/lib/kernel_roi.sh"

MODE_LABEL="PC mode (markerless, whole kernel)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Fixture: rt_c_v_matmul_free (markerless GEMM twin)"
echo "Trigger: ELF-derived vmatmul_kernel entry -> post-jal return PC"
echo "Window:  1 vmatmul_kernel call (one-shot trigger; remaining"
echo "         GEMM_REPEAT iterations run only on QEMU2)"
echo "=========================================================="

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf"
if [ ! -f "$ELF" ]; then
  echo "[demo pc] SKIP: $ELF missing (run make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf)"
  exit 77
fi

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
for tool in "$OBJDUMP" "$NM"; do
  if ! command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[demo pc] SKIP: $tool not found"
    exit 77
  fi
done

read -r ROI_START ROI_END < <(derive_kernel_roi "$ELF" "$OBJDUMP" "$NM") || true
if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] || [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
  echo "[demo pc] FAIL: could not derive kernel PCs from $ELF"
  exit 1
fi
echo "ROI start_pc = $ROI_START  (vmatmul_kernel entry)"
echo "ROI end_pc   = $ROI_END  (insn after jal vmatmul_kernel in main)"

set +e
FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul_free TRIGGER_MODE=pc EXPECT_RC=0 \
  ROI_START="$ROI_START" ROI_END="$ROI_END" \
  TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-120}" \
  bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/../e2e.sh"
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -eq 77 ]; then
  echo "[demo pc] SKIP (artifacts missing)"
  exit 77
fi

if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo pc] FAIL ($MODE_LABEL): underlying harness exit $RC"
  exit "$RC"
fi

echo "[demo pc] PASS ($MODE_LABEL)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RED-then-green test for derive_kernel_roi (tests/lib/kernel_roi.sh).
#
# Asserts the helper returns a PC pair that frames one full call of
# vmatmul_kernel: start = function entry, end = first insn after the
# `jal vmatmul_kernel` in main. Both must be hex addresses, end > start.
#
# Run manually:
#   bash tests/demos/test_demo_pc_oneshot_kernel.sh

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf"
if [ ! -f "$ELF" ]; then
  echo "[test_pc_kernel] SKIP: $ELF missing"
  exit 77
fi

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
for tool in "$OBJDUMP" "$NM"; do
  if ! command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[test_pc_kernel] SKIP: $tool not found"
    exit 77
  fi
done

LIB="$ROOT/tests/lib/kernel_roi.sh"
if [ ! -f "$LIB" ]; then
  echo "[test_pc_kernel] FAIL: $LIB does not exist yet"
  exit 1
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
. "$LIB"

if ! declare -F derive_kernel_roi >/dev/null; then
  echo "[test_pc_kernel] FAIL: derive_kernel_roi not defined in $LIB"
  exit 1
fi

read -r START END < <(derive_kernel_roi "$ELF" "$OBJDUMP" "$NM") || true
if [ -z "${START:-}" ] || [ -z "${END:-}" ]; then
  echo "[test_pc_kernel] FAIL: derive_kernel_roi returned empty PCs"
  exit 1
fi

case "$START" in 0x*) ;; *) echo "[test_pc_kernel] FAIL: start='$START' not 0x-prefixed"; exit 1 ;; esac
case "$END"   in 0x*) ;; *) echo "[test_pc_kernel] FAIL: end='$END' not 0x-prefixed"; exit 1 ;; esac

if (( END <= START )); then
  echo "[test_pc_kernel] FAIL: end ($END) must be > start ($START)"
  exit 1
fi

# Independent ground truth: start_pc must equal the nm symbol address of
# vmatmul_kernel; end_pc must equal the PC immediately following the
# `jal ...<vmatmul_kernel>` instruction inside main. Use here-strings
# (not `cmd | awk '... exit'` pipes) so awk's early exit does not raise
# SIGPIPE on the upstream tool, which `set -o pipefail` would surface as
# a test failure.
NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$ELF")
OBJ_OUT=$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$ELF")

WANT_START=0x$(awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print $1; exit}' <<< "$NM_OUT")
if [ "$WANT_START" != "$START" ]; then
  echo "[test_pc_kernel] FAIL: start=$START want $WANT_START (vmatmul_kernel entry)"
  exit 1
fi

WANT_END=$(awk '
  /^[0-9a-f]+ <main>:/ { in_main = 1; next }
  in_main && /^[0-9a-f]+ <[^>]+>:/ { in_main = 0 }
  in_main && saw_call { sub(":", "", $1); print "0x" $1; exit }
  in_main && $3 == "jal" && index($0, "<vmatmul_kernel>") { saw_call = 1 }
' <<< "$OBJ_OUT")
if [ -z "$WANT_END" ]; then
  echo "[test_pc_kernel] FAIL: could not locate `jal <vmatmul_kernel>` in main (independent check)"
  exit 1
fi
if [ "$WANT_END" != "$END" ]; then
  echo "[test_pc_kernel] FAIL: end=$END want $WANT_END (insn after jal vmatmul_kernel)"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[test_pc_kernel] PASS: derive_kernel_roi -> start=$START end=$END"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# derive_kernel_roi: derive the PC pair that frames one full call of the
# vsim-phase kernel (vmatmul_kernel) in an ELF, with no source-level
# markers required.
#
#   start_pc = symbol address of vmatmul_kernel (function entry)
#   end_pc   = PC of the instruction immediately following the
#              `jal ...<vmatmul_kernel>` site inside main (call-return PC)
#
# Used by PC-trigger demos against the markerless GEMM twin: the QEMU
# plugin's one-shot enter trigger fires when the hart retires the first
# insn at vmatmul_kernel; vsim's one-shot exit trigger fires when the hart
# is about to retire the post-jal insn in main. The measured window is
# therefore exactly one vmatmul_kernel call (16 outer rows x 16 inner
# k-iterations + prologue/epilogue + 16 vse32 stores), regardless of how
# many times main's GEMM_REPEAT loop is configured to invoke the kernel.
#
# Usage:
#   . tests/lib/kernel_roi.sh
#   read -r START END < <(derive_kernel_roi <elf> <objdump> <nm>)
#
# On success prints "0x<start> 0x<end>" (single line, space-separated) and
# returns 0. On miss prints nothing and returns 1.
#
# Implementation note: outputs are captured to variables first, then fed
# to awk via here-string. This avoids `cmd | awk '... exit'` pipes, which
# trigger SIGPIPE on the upstream producer and abort the caller when
# `set -o pipefail` is active.

derive_kernel_roi() {
  local elf="$1" objdump="$2" nm="$3"
  local nm_out obj_out start end

  nm_out=$("$nm" --defined-only "$elf" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  obj_out=$("$objdump" -d "$elf" 2>/dev/null) || return 1

  start=$(awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print $1; exit}' <<< "$nm_out")
  [ -n "$start" ] || return 1

  end=$(awk '
    /^[0-9a-f]+ <main>:/             { in_main = 1; next }
    in_main && /^[0-9a-f]+ <[^>]+>:/ { in_main = 0 }
    in_main && saw_call              { sub(":", "", $1); print $1; exit }
    in_main && $3 == "jal" && index($0, "<vmatmul_kernel>") { saw_call = 1 }
  ' <<< "$obj_out")
  [ -n "$end" ] || return 1

  printf '0x%s 0x%s\n' "$start" "$end"
}

# Demo (icount mode): instruction-count switching on the RVV GEMM workload.
#
# Whole-program mode: both legs drain by retired-instruction count alone, with
# no CSR markers in the workload:
#
#   QEMU1 + plugin icount=N1    -> drain at insn N1.
#   vsim --hybrid-icount N2     -> drain N2 insns later.
#
# Workload is the MARKERLESS GEMM twin rt_c_v_matmul_free (200 back-to-back
# 16x16x16 GEMMs, no csrwi 0x7C0). icount IS the only drain trigger -- the
# default CSR matcher has nothing to match. There is no natural end-of-program
# drain here (the demo stops vsim mid-kernel by count), so it asserts the
# round-trip DRAINS at both ends with both PCs landing inside vmatmul_kernel.
#
# Env (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU     qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN   libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_BIN      sim_<cpu>
#   VSIM_ELF      markerless fixture (default: rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf)
#   QEMU_ICOUNT   plugin icount drain target (default: 10000)
#   VSIM_ICOUNT   vsim icount drain target  (default: 5000)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul_free}"
QEMU_ICOUNT="${QEMU_ICOUNT:-10000}"
VSIM_ICOUNT="${VSIM_ICOUNT:-5000}"

MODE_LABEL="icount mode (samples a whole-program window)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Fixture: ${FIXTURE} (markerless RVV GEMM, 200 reps)"
echo "QEMU1 trigger: plugin icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT"
echo "vsim  trigger: --hybrid-icount $VSIM_ICOUNT  (CSR matcher disabled)"
echo "=========================================================="

hybrid_resolve_paths

# Resolve the GEMM kernel's address range so the drain checks assert the count
# target landed inside vmatmul_kernel (replaces the old icount_spin's hardcoded
# 0x100002/0x100004 loop PCs). readelf -sW: $2=value(hex) $3=size $8=name.
RE="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-readelf}"
RE="${RE:-riscv64-unknown-elf-readelf}"
read KLO KSZ < <("$RE" -sW "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '$8=="vmatmul_kernel"{print strtonum("0x"$2),$3; exit}')
if [ -z "${KLO:-}" ] || [ -z "${KSZ:-}" ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: could not resolve vmatmul_kernel range from $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1
fi
pc_in_kernel() { awk -v p="$1" -v lo="$KLO" -v sz="$KSZ" 'BEGIN{exit !(p>=lo && p<lo+sz)}'; }
echo "  vmatmul_kernel: $(printf '0x%x..0x%x' "$KLO" "$((KLO+KSZ))")"

SHM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-icount-rt.XXXXXX)
STATE_Q=$(mktemp)
STATE_V=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
VSIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHM" "$STATE_Q" "$STATE_V" "$QEMU_LOG" "$VSIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHM_SIZE" "$SHM"

read_u64() { python3 -c "
import struct
with open('$1', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek($2); print(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0])
"; }

echo "[demo icount 1/2] QEMU1 + plugin icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT -> drain"
set +e
timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHM,size=$SHM_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_Q,icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT" \
  >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
QRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: QEMU1 expected exit 200, got $QRC"
  tail -20 "$QEMU_LOG"; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_Q" ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: QEMU1 state empty"; exit 1
fi

PC_Q=$(read_u64 "$STATE_Q" 16)
if ! pc_in_kernel "$PC_Q"; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: QEMU1 drained pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_Q") not in vmatmul_kernel"; exit 1
fi
echo "  QEMU1 drain: pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_Q") (in kernel)"

# vsim resumes from the QEMU drain and attaches the SAME shared mmap so the
# GEMM matrices QEMU1 wrote to .bss survive (mirrors tests/e2e.sh).
echo "[demo icount 2/2] vsim --hybrid-icount $VSIM_ICOUNT -> drain"
set +e
timeout 120 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_Q" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_V" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHM_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --hybrid-icount "$VSIM_ICOUNT" \
  >"$VSIM_LOG" 2>&1
VRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$VRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: vsim expected exit 200, got $VRC"
  tail -20 "$VSIM_LOG"; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_V" ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: vsim state empty"; exit 1
fi

PC_V=$(read_u64 "$STATE_V" 16)
if ! pc_in_kernel "$PC_V"; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: vsim drained pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_V") not in vmatmul_kernel"; exit 1
fi
echo "  vsim drain: pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_V") (in kernel)"

# Window cycles: the vsim mcycle delta over the measured window (mcycle@624).
# vsim restores mcycle from the QEMU drain then counts real cycles, so
# vsim - qemu is the window's cycle count.
MC_Q=$(read_u64 "$STATE_Q" 624)
MC_V=$(read_u64 "$STATE_V" 624)
echo "  window_cycles: $((MC_V - MC_Q))  (vsim mcycle=$MC_V - qemu mcycle=$MC_Q)"

echo "[demo icount] PASS ($MODE_LABEL): both drains inside vmatmul_kernel"
